topics.name: Introduction to C Programming
subtopics: History Features and Applications of C
Role of C in System Programming

questions.title: Integer Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read a single integer from standard input and print it back on its own line.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print the integer N on its own line.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Character Echo Drill
questions.description:
Read a single character from standard input and print it back on its own line.

Input Format:
A single character C.

Output Format:
Print the character C on its own line.

Constraints:
C is a printable ASCII character.
questions.inputconstrains: C is a printable ASCII character

questions.title: Float Two Decimal Echo
questions.description:
Read a double value and print it formatted to exactly two decimal places.

Input Format:
A single floating-point number X.

Output Format:
Print X with exactly two digits after the decimal point.

Constraints:
-1000000.0 <= X <= 1000000.0

questions.title: Two Integer Order Swap Display
questions.description:
Read two integers and print them first in the order received, then on a second line in swapped order.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers A and B.

Output Format:
Line 1: A B
Line 2: B A

Constraints:
-1000000 <= A, B <= 1000000

questions.title: Name Banner Printer
questions.description:
Read a single-word name and print it wrapped in a banner of equals signs.

Input Format:
A single-word string NAME (no spaces).

Output Format:
Print the line "=== NAME ===" exactly.

Constraints:
1 <= length(NAME) <= 50

questions.title: Integer Float Pair Echo
questions.description:
Read an integer and a floating-point value and print them on separate lines, the integer first, the float formatted to two decimals second.

Input Format:
A line containing an integer N and a floating-point X separated by a space.

Output Format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: X formatted with exactly two decimal places.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= N <= 1000000 and -1000000.0 <= X <= 1000000.0

questions.title: Cafe Order Receipt Printer
questions.description:
A small cafe prints a basic receipt for every order. Read the item name and its price, then print a two-line receipt.

Input Format:
Line 1: a single-word item name ITEM.
Line 2: the price PRICE as a floating-point number.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Item: <ITEM>"
Line 2: "Price: <PRICE>" with PRICE formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= length(ITEM) <= 50 and 0.0 <= PRICE <= 100000.0

questions.title: Library Member Card Profile
questions.description:
The city library issues a numeric ID and a single-word member name. Print a one-line profile that combines them.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer member ID.
Line 2: single-word member NAME.

Output Format:
Print "Member #<ID>: <NAME>" on a single line.

Constraints:
0 <= ID <= 1000000 and 1 <= length(NAME) <= 50

questions.title: Celsius Temperature Display
questions.description:
A weather station reads a temperature in degrees Celsius and prints it in a fixed-format line.

Input Format:
A single floating-point value C representing degrees Celsius.

Output Format:
Print "T = <C> C" with C formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
-100.0 <= C <= 200.0

questions.title: Student Grade Card Printer
questions.description:
A school prints a three-line grade card for every student. Read the roll number, single-word name, and marks (out of 100) and print them as a formatted card.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer roll number.
Line 2: single-word NAME.
Line 3: floating-point marks.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Roll: <roll>"
Line 2: "Name: <NAME>"
Line 3: "Marks: <marks>" with marks formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= roll <= 1000000, 1 <= length(NAME) <= 50, 0.0 <= marks <= 100.0

questions.title: Warehouse Pallet Quantity Reporter
questions.description:
A warehouse supervisor walks the aisles counting pallets. For each pallet she records a code and the quantity of items on it. After touring N pallets she wants a quick summary: how many pallets she counted and the total quantity across all of them.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of pallets).
Next N lines: two space-separated integers CODE and QTY.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Pallets: <N>"
Line 2: "Total Qty: <sum of QTY>"

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= CODE <= 100000, 1 <= QTY <= 100000

questions.title: Constant Circle Metrics Calculator
questions.description:
A mechanical drafting tool uses a compile-time constant for PI to compute the circumference and area of a circle from a given radius. Use a #define constant for PI equal to 3.14159 and print both metrics to two decimals.

Input Format:
A single floating-point value R representing the radius.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Circumference: <C>" with two decimals.
Line 2: "Area: <A>" with two decimals.

Constraints:
0.0 <= R <= 10000.0

questions.title: Sensor Reading Averager
questions.description:
An embedded system samples a voltage sensor five times per cycle and reports the average. Read exactly five voltage readings and print the average to two decimal places.

Input Format:
Five lines, each containing one floating-point voltage value.

Output Format:
Print "Average: <avg>" with avg formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
0.0 <= voltage <= 12.0

questions.title: Static Counter Lifetime Demo
questions.description:
A controller increments a file-scope counter N times and reports the final value, demonstrating that the counter retains its lifetime across function calls. Read N and print the resulting counter.

Input Format:
A single integer N.

Output Format:
Print "Counter: <N>" on its own line.

Constraints:
0 <= N <= 1000000

questions.title: Train Coach Numbering Sequence
questions.description:
A railway yard assigns consecutive coach numbers starting from a given first number. Given the starting coach number and the count of coaches, print each coach number on its own line. Use a const-qualified variable for the step between coaches.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: FIRST (the starting coach number) and N (the count of coaches).

Output Format:
Print N lines, each containing one coach number, starting from FIRST and incrementing by 1.

Constraints:
1 <= FIRST <= 100000, 1 <= N <= 1000

questions.title: ATM Receipt Header Builder
questions.description:
An ATM prints a receipt header containing a customer name bracketed by lines of equals signs. Read the customer name from a single line and print the header.

Input Format:
A single line containing the customer NAME (may contain spaces).

Output Format:
Print exactly four lines:
"========================"
"ATM RECEIPT"
"Customer: <NAME>"
"========================"

Constraints:
1 <= length(NAME) <= 80

questions.title: Employee Pay Slip Generator
questions.description:
A payroll clerk prepares pay slips for several employees. For each employee she reads a single-word name and a basic salary, then computes the house-rent allowance (10% of basic), dearness allowance (5% of basic) and gross pay. Use const-qualified constants for the allowance percentages. Print one pay slip line per employee.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (employee count).
Next N lines: each contains a single-word NAME and a floating-point BASIC salary, space-separated.

Output Format:
For each employee print exactly one line:
"<NAME>: Basic <B> HRA <H> DA <D> Gross <G>"
with B, H, D, G each formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= length(NAME) <= 50, 0.0 <= BASIC <= 1000000.0
questions.sampleoutput1:
Alice: Basic 5000.00 HRA 500.00 DA 250.00 Gross 5750.00
Bob: Basic 8000.00 HRA 800.00 DA 400.00 Gross 9200.00

questions.title: Library Loan Fine Calculator
questions.description:
A municipal library charges overdue fines using a tiered policy: 0 rupees for 0 days late, 2 rupees per day for the first 10 days, and 5 rupees per day for every day beyond 10. Read the number of overdue books followed by (book_id, days_late) pairs and print the total fine collected.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of books).
Next N lines: two space-separated integers BOOK_ID and DAYS_LATE.

Output Format:
Print "Total Fine: <amount>" on its own line.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= BOOK_ID <= 1000000, 0 <= DAYS_LATE <= 1000

questions.title: Inventory Restock Value Reporter
questions.description:
A store manager tallies the restock value of N items. For each item she records a numeric code, a quantity, and a unit price. She wants a per-item line plus the grand total at the end.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of items).
Next N lines: three space-separated values CODE (int), QTY (int), PRICE (double).

Output Format:
For each item print: "Code <CODE> Qty <QTY> Total <T>" with T formatted to two decimals.
After all items, print: "Grand Total: <G>" with G formatted to two decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 1000, 1 <= CODE <= 1000000, 0 <= QTY <= 10000, 0.0 <= PRICE <= 10000.0
questions.sampleoutput1:
Code 1 Qty 10 Total 50.00
Code 2 Qty 5 Total 10.00
Grand Total: 60.00
questions.output2:
Code 10 Qty 2 Total 10.00
Code 20 Qty 3 Total 12.00
Code 30 Qty 4 Total 10.00
Grand Total: 32.00
questions.output3:
Code 1 Qty 100 Total 50.00
Code 2 Qty 50 Total 75.00
Grand Total: 125.00

questions.title: Battery Voltage Range Classifier
questions.description:
A battery management system reads N voltage readings and classifies each reading as Low (strictly below 3.0 V), Normal (3.0 V up to and including 4.2 V), or High (strictly above 4.2 V). At the end it reports the three counts.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer N (number of readings).
Next N lines: a single floating-point voltage value.

Output Format:
Line 1: "Low: <count>"
Line 2: "Normal: <count>"
Line 3: "High: <count>"

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100000, 0.0 <= voltage <= 12.0
